existing approved source watchlist and prior versions

inputs: source-linked candidate changes for review
actual complete authority texts
outputs: technologist-checked relevant changes and uncertainties

steps.what: Assess implications for the actual healthcare system privacy and security controls
inputs: technologist-checked relevant changes and uncertainties
actual healthcare system and control inventory
outputs: technologist impact assessment and needed specialist questions

technologist-checked relevant changes and uncertainties

tasks.design: Configure native source subscriptions and exact version comparison in {COMPLIANCE_LIBRARY}, denoted OTHER alongside the actual control inventory. Reduce repeated source collection only. The technologist reads provisions and assesses impact. Final written record approval and same-system save are separate; save receives no benefit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeatedly checking selected authority pages for a new version may consume collection effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Native subscriptions and version comparisons can surface actual source changes.
tasks.still_hard: Applicability and implications for actual healthcare information controls.
tasks.human_edge: The technologist understands the implemented system and when legal/security expertise is needed.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: selected authority subscriptions and document version comparisons can reduce repeated change collection without interpreting legal effect.

assumptions: Shares are provisional; verify remaining manual collection after current subscriptions and watch tools. Existing feeds earn no new saving.

Authority publishers supply actual notice_id, published_date and source_version; the technologist checks the approved source watchlist and retains source/effective-date checking in s1-s2. Unsupported feeds or missing old versions require manual checking; no change or effective date is invented.

s4 captures actual source_reference, assessed_control, impact and unresolved_question at full time. This is monitoring, not an automatic legal determination or hidden policy notification. Same-system save stays full.

approved native schema and access templates

actual approved test records and access cases

tasks.design: Configure {HEALTH_RECORD_PLATFORM} native schemas, index mappings and access templates, denoted OTHER. Work on candidate configuration and record sets before the final gated commit. Reuse exact existing source classifications only; ambiguous free text stays manual. Full retrieval/permission testing remains human. Commit runtime and save action earn no benefit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Index setup and exact record classification may repeat existing schema and source fields manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates and validated exact mappings can reduce those repeated operations.
tasks.still_hard: Reliable patient linkage, correct access and detecting incomplete retrieval.
tasks.human_edge: The technologist understands clinical record meaning and consequences of wrong linkage.
tasks.altitude: Technologist-owned health indexes with native exact mappings.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: health record platforms can configure schemas, access templates and exact source-field index mappings.

assumptions: All shares are provisional for a setup/operation cycle; measure actual mix and residual manual work after current platform features. Existing database query/index runtime earns no new saving.

Clinicians and registration systems already produce patient_id, encounter_id, document_type, event_date and approved classification_code in normal records. s1 retains full field meaning/linkage verification; missing or conflicting fields require manual work. No new upstream coding is assumed.

s2 retains 15 hours for configuration choices; s3 retains complete collection/retrieval/access tests and correction; s4 retains 8 hours for exception inspection. Candidate sets are not live writes until s6; missing native staging support requires manual controlled changes.

s5 approves the actual exact version and record set after tests. This instance assumes existing delegated production authority; otherwise retain the actual platform owners approval. Same-system commit stays full.
unknowns: Native staging and index configuration support

tasks.short: Prepare statistical and narrative reports and graphics from health registry information.

steps.what: Verify registry cohort, actual data completeness, reporting purpose and authorised audience
inputs: actual registry records and data dictionary
actual approved reporting request and access scope
outputs: registrar-checked report cohort, fields and disclosure scope

steps.what: Generate exact statistical tables and graphic presentations using approved native registry report definitions
inputs: registrar-checked report cohort, fields and disclosure scope
approved actual report definitions and disclosure rules
outputs: source-linked registry tables and graphics draft

steps.what: Draft and correct the narrative against actual registry figures, definitions and missing-data limitations
inputs: source-linked registry tables and graphics draft
registrar-checked report cohort, fields and disclosure scope
actual registry definitions and limitations
outputs: complete corrected registry report draft

loop.purpose: Describe actual registry tables without inferring clinical causes or unobserved outcomes
loop.input: checked actual tables, cohort definitions and documented limitations
loop.output: candidate narrative linked to exact figures and definitions
loop.check: Registrar checks every figure, denominator, cohort, period, omission, missing-data caveat and disclosure against original records; corrects all text
loop.stop: Untraceable number, unsupported clinical inference or two failed corrections returns writing to registrar
loop.why_not_simpler: Native reports generate exact figures first; variable narrative wording needs semantic drafting and complete correction

steps.what: Approve the complete final statistical report, narrative, graphics and exact permitted recipients
inputs: complete corrected registry report draft
registrar-checked report cohort, fields and disclosure scope
outputs: approved final registry report and exact internal recipients

steps.what: Save the approved final registry report
inputs: approved final registry report and exact internal recipients
outputs: saved final registry report

steps.what: Send the approved final registry report to its approved internal users
inputs: saved final registry report
approved final registry report and exact internal recipients
outputs: dispatched final registry report
steps.handoff_to: authorised internal hospital staff or researchers

tasks.design: Configure native {REGISTRY_SYSTEM} reports and charts, denoted OTHER, before a bounded narrative loop. Registrar verifies cohort and disclosure scope, corrects every narrative claim and approves the complete final report before separate save and internal dispatch. Save/send stay fully retained.
tasks.previous_blocker: Actual registry tables and charts may be manually assembled alongside report wording.
tasks.enabler_now: Native report definitions can reuse exact registry fields; source-grounded drafting can assist descriptions.
tasks.still_hard: Cohort validity, data completeness and avoiding misleading or disclosive conclusions.
tasks.human_edge: The registrar understands coding definitions and limitations of the collected data.
tasks.altitude: Registrar-owned statistics and narrative with traceable exact figures.

evidence.claim: Healthcare registry pipelines and returned statistics support deterministic report preparation from existing registered data.
Model knowledge: a bounded draft can describe checked registry tables but needs complete registrar correction.

assumptions: All shares are provisional; credit only residual manual table/graphic assembly and corrected wording after current native registry reports. Existing pipelines and calculations earn no new benefit.

Registry capture already supplies normal patient/episode keys, diagnosis/classification, event_dates and followup_status from clinicians/registrars. s1 retains complete cohort, data quality and disclosure checks; missing values remain explicit, never inferred. Existing authorised reporting request supplies actual audience and purpose.

s3 retains 15 hours for complete semantic correction and s4 retains 25 for final statistical/privacy review. Internal staff/researcher audience is assumed here; any external researcher dispatch needs act_external authority and actual disclosure approval. Same-system save and send earn no benefit.
research_questions: Which registry tables or graphics are still manually assembled after current native reports?

incremental.description: Audit narrative/statistical errors and maintain cohort/report mappings

approvals.approved_version: s4 complete final registry report and permitted cohort
s4 complete final registry report and exact permitted internal users

tasks.design: Configure native source links in {CODING_WORKLIST}, denoted OTHER with the clinical record. Reduce retrieval only. Registrar frames the neutral question and approves its complete final version before separate send, then consults people and writes a supported correction after the actual response. Code commit stays separate and fully retained; no model invents a diagnosis.
tasks.previous_blocker: Locating all conflicting source entries may require repeated navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native coding worklist links can retrieve the actual source entries together.
tasks.still_hard: Resolving clinical ambiguity and applying coding guidance to a supported diagnosis.
tasks.human_edge: The registrar knows when clinician clarification is necessary and preserves unresolved status honestly.
tasks.altitude: Human coding clarification with actual source retrieval.

evidence.claim: Coding support exists, but this design uses native record links and retains every ambiguous clinical/coding decision.

assumptions: All shares are provisional; confirm residual source retrieval after current coding worklist functions. Existing suggested codes earn no saving here.

Clinical authors supply actual signed diagnosis entries and source timestamps; registrar captures the actual discrepancy in s2 at full time. s1 retains source checking; missing source linkage uses manual retrieval.

s3 captures/checks actual request, patient identity and internal recipient before send. s6 captures actual clinician_clarification, source_reference, chosen_code or unresolved_status at full time after consultation. A consultation does not guarantee a resolved diagnosis. Every changed request/correction returns to its final approval. Same-system commit and send earn no saving.
